summary: Read all of record 14 (Neutrals and the kingdom), all 123 provinces in record 30 (index 0 is a placeholder: 123 shires, not 124), record 13 (3 cultures), record 31 (43 default name bases), record 1 lore/calendar, and the cells' state/province/culture arrays (records 25/27/19, with geometry from the live FMG pack). AGREE: kingdom form Monarchy/Kingdom 'Rìoghachd Dia-thìris' (V-0007), capital Cathair dhearg (burg 19, centre = its cell), culture Dia-thìrich, no foreign neighbours or diplomacy (V-0011); lore Diosal Era, 2026 (Appendix D); all 505 burgs in state 1, every burg's culture matches its cell and the gazetteer (441 Dia-thìrich / 64 Tuathaich, 543,205 Tuathaich townsfolk, as F says); 13 shires named from Seann roots and 30 Seann burgs (F); all 29 moved towns (burg_moves.json) are still in the province their gazetteer/in-files give (0 mismatches over all 505 burgs); every other gazetteer 'seat of its province' claim (about 80) matches the province's seat burg; all annal province: refs and 'Siorrachd X' names exist. CONFLICTS (fixed): 123 generator formNames (Province/Governorate/Prefecture/Department/Island(s)/Area) -> 'Siorrachd'; provinces 122/123 had no seat and doubled names ('Siorrachd Siorrachd fhionn/àrsaidh') -> named for their one-cell islands Eilean dhìreach / Eilean ìseal (coordinate with the heraldry pass, which also touches their fullName: take these values); one land cell (4281, Eilean gheal) was culture 0 Seann-Dhaoine with 2,167 people although F says the Old Ones are gone -> Dia-thìrich, culture stats adjusted; all cultures used the English name base -> new 'Dia-thìris' base 43 of the island's 245 burg names; culture codes Ki/Ma -> Tu/Rò; Seann-Dhaoine type Generic -> Naval (F: a coastal people); 12 province centres still on moved seats' old cells (optional); gazetteer: burgs 54 and 352 claimed to be seats but are not (seats 244 and 198), 387 'principal city' of Seann Tarr's shire, 365 'royal seat in the Holy Age' against Appendix A (seat at Dùn dhearg then Cathair dhearg); F said 'two Baile chrom' (map has four). MISSING (written): Appendix H (new file) with the kingdom, how the shires came to be (Holy Age provinces, Sundering shires, humans' districts, the drawing of V-0014), the shape of the shires (11 doubled names, island shires, scattered shires 120/121 and four island/exclave shires, 5 seats smaller than another town, the 11 Tuathaich shires, one kind of shire), the Crown's dues and Treasury (salesTax 0.17 = market-due 17 in 100; pollTax 0.18 = 18 purses per 100,000 heads on 36,225,000 heads; treasury 9,568.04 = 6,520.51 head-due + 3,047.53 market-due), the unclaimed Neutral land (81 cells, two pieces of the NW frozen shore, all Tuathaich, glacier, 397,430 rural, no burgs, bordering only province 120; the map's campaign defender) and why no one holds it, culture extents (Dia-thìrich 2,404 cells / ~84.6% of land, Tuathaich 536 / ~15.4% incl. the unclaimed 1.7%), and a table of all 123 shires with seat, burgs, people, seat's age and notes; 7 annals (IV-0246a district of the outer coasts; V-0014a frozen coast left out; V-0014b island shires; V-0015a dues set; V-0139a Doire chaol shire, since its seat was founded after 1932; VI-0098a holdouts onto the frozen coast; VI-0154a Treasury roll 2026); 2 gazetteer appends (127 Seann Vell's scattered shire, 164 Doire chaol); text edits in F, E and book V. Counts: map edits 153 (123 formName + 4 names + 12 centres + 1 cell + 12 culture fields + 1 name base); annals 7 added; gazetteer 8; text 6; new file 1. Areas in Appendix H use the agreed scale of 0.2 miles per map unit (0.04 sq mi per unit of area): island 272,668 units = ~10,900 sq mi; shires 267,917 = ~10,720; frozen coast 4,751 = ~190; Dia-thìrich 230,591 = ~9,220; Tuathaich 42,077 = ~1,680. No distances are written.

event.title: The district of the outer coasts
event.body: The Administration makes the outer coasts a single district and governs it from the harbour office at Seann Vell on Eilean ruadh, where its revenue cutters lie: the islands of the west and south, Eilean bhàn with Cuan dhearg and Cnoc chaol, and the southern edge of the ice in the far north-west. Its surveyors walk the ice margin and go no farther. Beyond it the district map is left blank.

event.title: The frozen coast left out
event.body: The shire lines stop where the humans' survey stopped, at the ice margin of the far north-west. The frozen coast beyond, an Oirthir Reòthte, with its sealers and fowlers, is put in no shire and given no maor. The council's minute says only that it 'is not in the survey'.

event.title: The island shires
event.body: Two rocks that each kept a customs station of the Administration, Eilean dhìreach off the Tuathaich coast and Eilean ìseal off the east coast, are kept as shires of their own, since the council has no rule for folding a district into its neighbour. Neither has a town to name it, and each shire takes its island's name.

event.title: The Crown's dues set
event.body: The council sets the dues the maoir are to collect: a head-due, cìs-cinn, on every household by the number of its heads, and a market-due, cìs-margaidh, on every sale made by a seller of the kingdom. The humans' harbour tariff at Ros dhomhain stays in force until the kingdom has a coin of its own to take the market-due in.

event.title: Siorrachd Doire chaol
event.body: Doire chaol, the village laid out south of the capital for the families of the royal household, has grown too large for the maor of Baile chiar to govern from his seat. The council cuts it out as a shire of its own, the only shire made since the drawing.

event.title: Onto the frozen coast
event.body: Some of the holdouts of Cnoc thais go on past the hills and out onto the frozen coast of the far north-west. The regiments follow them to the edge of the shire of Seann Vell and no farther. The open record names them, as it names every enemy of the war, only as those 'of no shire'.

event.title: The Treasury's roll of the present year
event.body: The Treasury's roll for the year stands at 9,568 purses: 6,521 from the head-due, taken at eighteen purses on every hundred thousand heads, and 3,047 from the market-due, taken at seventeen in the hundred on every sale. The wartime tithe is carried on its own line under the regiments' pay. The frozen coast pays neither due.

gazetteer_edit.old: Muileann àrsaidh, the ancient mill, is the seat of its province in the Tuathaich north-west, founded as a Dia-thìrich mill town in the Holy Age.
gazetteer_edit.new: Muileann àrsaidh, the ancient mill, is the younger of the two Muileann àrsaidh in the Tuathaich north-west, founded as a Dia-thìrich mill town in the Holy Age; the seat of the shire is the elder town close by.
gazetteer_edit.why: The seat of province 105 is burg 244 (the elder Muileann àrsaidh), not 54.

gazetteer_edit.old: Cnoc dhubh is the seat of its province, a walled market for the herders and quarrymen of the hills near Làrach an Teampaill.
gazetteer_edit.new: Cnoc dhubh is a walled market for the herders and quarrymen of the hills near Làrach an Teampaill; the seat of the shire is the other Cnoc dhubh, the charcoal-burners' town.
gazetteer_edit.why: The seat of province 110 is burg 198, not 352.

gazetteer_edit.old: Baile Mòr ruadh is a walled city of red stone, crowned by a citadel, and the principal city of its province.
gazetteer_edit.new: Baile Mòr ruadh is a walled city of red stone, crowned by a citadel, and the strongest place of its province, though the seat of the shire is the old harbour of Seann Tarr.
gazetteer_edit.why: Province 60's seat is Seann Tarr (burg 249), which is also larger; 'principal city' read as the seat.

gazetteer_edit.old: It was fought over in the Age of Strangers, when the human administration made it a district seat, and its walls show repairs of every age.
gazetteer_edit.new: It was fought over in the Age of Strangers, when the human administration made it a district seat, and when the shires were drawn the seat went back to Seann Tarr. Its walls show repairs of every age.
gazetteer_edit.why: Explains why the humans' district seat is not the shire seat (Appendix H § II).

gazetteer_edit.old: It was a royal seat in the Holy Age and a centre of the human administration in the Age of Strangers.
gazetteer_edit.new: It held one of the royal granaries in the Holy Age and was a centre of the human administration in the Age of Strangers.
gazetteer_edit.why: Appendix A: the Holy Age seat of the rìghrean was Dùn dhearg, then Cathair dhearg (II-0135); no royal seat at Baile Mòr mhòr. Granaries in every province seat (II-0170).

gazetteer_edit.old: the early kings of the northern province
gazetteer_edit.new: the granary-keepers of the early kings in the north
gazetteer_edit.why: Same: no separate northern kings in Appendix A.

gazetteer_edit.new: Its shire is the humans' old district of the outer coasts, kept whole: the islands of the west and south, Eilean bhàn with Cuan dhearg and Cnoc chaol, and the southern edge of the frozen coast in the far north-west.
gazetteer_edit.why: Province 120 is scattered (seat on one-cell Eilean ruadh; Eilean bhàn with two towns in the south; Eilean ghorm; 89 cells of the NW ice margin with no town). Explained in IV-0246a and Appendix H.

gazetteer_edit.old: It grew into a large village and the seat of its province.
gazetteer_edit.new: It grew into a large village, and in the kingdom's fourth decade it was cut out of the shire of Baile chiar as a shire of its own, the only shire made since the drawing.
gazetteer_edit.why: Seat founded 1932-1960 (after the shires were drawn in 1932): shire 67 must have been made later (V-0139a).

text_edit.new:

of its seat, or, where it has no town, of its island (Appendix H). Names repeat freely; there are four Baile chrom and four Seann Skell, and the rolls
text_edit.why: Two island shires have no seat (V-0014b); the map has four Baile chrom (burgs 187, 189, 305, 381), as the gazetteer of burg 381 already says.

text_edit.old: some 543,000 people in them. The Dia-thìrich hold the other 441. The largest Tuathaich towns:
text_edit.new: some 543,000 people in them. The Dia-thìrich hold the other 441. The Tuathaich country is some fifteen parts in a hundred of the island's land, the frozen coast of the far north-west among it, and the Dia-thìrich country the other eighty-five (Appendix H). The largest Tuathaich towns:
text_edit.why: Culture extents (cells: Dia-thìrich 2,404, Tuathaich 536 incl. 81 unclaimed; area 230,591 / 42,077 of 272,668).

text_edit.old: The kingdom redrew the shires on the humans' district lines ({{date:V-0014}}).
text_edit.new: The kingdom redrew the shires on the humans' district lines ({{date:V-0014}}), and has had a hundred and twenty-three since {{year:V-0139a}} (Appendix H).

text_edit.old: A *maor* was set over each shire to collect the Crown's dues.
text_edit.new: A *maor* was set over each shire to collect the Crown's dues: the head-due on every household by its heads, and the market-due on every sale. Where the humans' lines stopped, at the ice margin of the far north-west, the shires stopped too, and the frozen coast beyond was left in no shire at all.
text_edit.why: Taxes (record 14 salesTax/pollTax) and the Neutral lands (state 0) had no place in the book.

text_edit.old: The open record gives the number of holdouts taken and not the number who went on into the hills.
text_edit.new: The open record gives the number of holdouts taken and not the number who went on into the hills. Some of those went on past the hills onto the frozen coast, beyond the shire lines, and the regiments did not follow them there.
text_edit.why: Ties the campaign's defender (state 0, the unclaimed) to the Neutral lands (VI-0098a).

text_edit.old: the coinage is pegged to it, and the tithe is taken on every sale.
text_edit.new: the coinage is pegged to it, and the tithe is taken on every sale. The Treasury's roll for the year stood at 9,568 purses, two parts in three of it from the head-due.

unsure: Coordinator note checked: the islands Eilean ghorm, Eilean dhubh and Eilean gheal are NOT in the Neutrals: every island cell is state 1 (Eilean ghorm in province 120, Eilean dhubh in 119, Eilean gheal in 121). The only state-0 land is 81 cells of the main island (feature 2) in the far north-west, in two pieces (76 cells round x171,y127 and 5 cells round x254,y113).

Province 120 (Seann Vell of the west) is left scattered on the map and explained in the history (the humans' 'district of the outer coasts', IV-0246a) rather than re-drawn: reassigning its 89 north-western cells would also need the saved SVG province borders redrawn. If the integrator prefers a map fix, the NW piece could go to province 105 (Muileann àrsaidh) or to the Neutrals; then H § III/V, IV-0246a, V-0014a and gazetteer 127 need their outer-coast wording trimmed.

Population on the ice: the Neutral cells hold 397,430 rural people and the NW piece of province 120 771,425, on glacier/tundra (habitability 0). The history hedges the Neutral figure as 'the Moot's tallies ... which the royal clerks do not accept'. Lowering those cells' pop (record 21) would be the map-side alternative.

Culture origins: FMG roots every culture at culture 0 (origins [0]), so the tree reads Tuathaich and Dia-thìrich as 'from the Seann-Dhaoine'. The loader forces this; left as it is. The history (F) stays agnostic on descent, and the Tuathaich descend from the humans.
State 0 keeps the name 'Neutrals' (it also covers the sea). It could be renamed 'An Oirthir Reòthte' if the integrator wants the unclaimed land named in the states editor.
world.json still has province 122/123 as 'Siorrachd fhionn'/'Siorrachd àrsaidh'. H does not use {{place:province:122/123}} tokens, but world.json should be regenerated after the map edit.

The campaign record (An Cogadh Fada, attacker 1, defender 0) belongs to the military pass. The history here calls the enemy 'those of no shire' (VI-0098a, H § V), which fits their reading ('unaffiliated holdouts').
Outside this layer: gazetteer burg 9 (Inis mhin) gives founded_age III, but II-0200 records the town in the Holy Age.
The rates (17% and 18%) are given as present-year figures, with no date for when they were set. V-0015a sets the kinds of dues in 1933 and gives no rates.
